original_value: AbstractFigurative language (FL) seems ubiquitous in all social media discussion forums and chats, posing extra challenges to sentiment analysis endeavors. Identification of FL schemas in short texts remains largely an unresolved issue in the broader field of natural language processing, mainly due to their contradictory and metaphorical meaning content. The main FL expression forms are sarcasm, irony and metaphor. In the present paper, we employ advanced deep learning methodologies to tackle the problem of identifying the aforementioned FL forms. Significantly extending our previous work (Potamias et al., in: International conference on engineering applications of neural networks, Springer, Berlin, pp 164–175, 2019), we propose a neural network methodology that builds on a recently proposed pre-trained transformer-based network architecture which is further enhanced with the employment and devise of a recurrent convolutional neural network. With this setup, data preprocessing is kept in minimum. The performance of the devised hybrid neural architecture is tested on four benchmark datasets, and contrasted with other relevant state-of-the-art methodologies and systems. Results demonstrate that the proposed methodology achieves state-of-the-art performance under all benchmark datasets, outperforming, even by a large margin, all other methodologies and published studies.

result.paraphrase: Figurative language (FL) appears to be pervasive across social media discussion forums and chats, creating additional difficulty for sentiment analysis efforts. Detecting FL schemas in short texts remains largely unresolved in the broader natural language processing field, mainly because of their contradictory and metaphorical meaning. The principal FL forms are sarcasm, irony, and metaphor. In this paper, we use advanced deep learning methods to address the task of identifying these FL forms. Building substantially on our previous work (Potamias et al., in: International conference on engineering applications of neural networks, Springer, Berlin, pp 164–175, 2019), we introduce a neural network approach based on a recently proposed pre-trained transformer network architecture, further enhanced by a recurrent convolutional neural network. In this configuration, data preprocessing is kept to a minimum. The proposed hybrid neural architecture is evaluated on four benchmark datasets and compared with other relevant state-of-the-art methods and systems. The results show that the proposed method attains state-of-the-art performance on all benchmark datasets, surpassing all other methods and published studies, in some cases by a wide margin.
